SOIL 500.faculty: Faculty of Land and Food Systems
SOIL 500.description: This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

SOIL 501.faculty: Faculty of Land and Food Systems
SOIL 501.description: Integrating the environmental factors influencing soil-forming processes and their ecological implications. Credit will be granted for only one of SOIL_V 501 or APBI_V 401. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

SOIL 502.faculty: Faculty of Land and Food Systems
SOIL 502.description: Integration of fundamental, unifying, soil science principles in sustainable ecosystem management. Credit will be granted for only one of SOIL_V 502 or APBI_V 402. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

SOIL 503.course_name: Advanced Soil Sampling, Analyses and Data Interpretation
SOIL 503.faculty: Faculty of Land and Food Systems
SOIL 503.description: Field and laboratory analytical techniques in the chemical, biological and physical assessment of soils. Credit will be granted for only one of SOIL_V 503 or APBI_V 403. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

SOIL 512.faculty: Faculty of Land and Food Systems
SOIL 512.description: Current research in root-soil interfaces. Offered in alternate years. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

SOIL 513.faculty: Faculty of Land and Food Systems
SOIL 513.description: Infiltration and evaporation of water, flow and storage of heat and chemicals in soil, and interactions with the atmosphere. Emphasis on mathematical formulation of problems and solutions using analytical and numerical methods. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

SOIL 514.faculty: Faculty of Land and Food Systems
SOIL 514.description: Energy and mass exchange in the biosphere with emphasis on the interfaces between the atmosphere and soils, plants and animals. Offered in alternate years. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

SOIL 515.faculty: Faculty of Land and Food Systems
SOIL 515.description: Watershed evaluation, key aspects of hydrology, water quality, land use impacts on water resources and integration of multiple land use activities and their cumulative impacts. Equivalency: LWS_V 515. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

SOIL 516.faculty: Faculty of Land and Food Systems
SOIL 516.description: Urbanization impacts on water resources with a focus on rainwater management, water quality, point and non-point sources of pollution, drinking water and waste water, riparian buffer zones, cumulative effects, and application of beneficial management practices. Equivalency: LWS_V 516. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

SOIL 517.faculty: Faculty of Land and Food Systems
SOIL 517.description: Topics in land and water system evaluations and assessing resource development options; monitoring and modelling environmental systems. Equivalency: LWS_V 517. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

SOIL 518.faculty: Faculty of Land and Food Systems
SOIL 518.description: Key water issues associated with international development: global water demand, scarcity, efficiency of use, water as a commodity, biophysical and policy aspects of water management, water and health, land use impact, water harvesting, improved irrigation, and pollution prevention. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

SOIL 520.faculty: Faculty of Land and Food Systems
SOIL 520.description: Intensive and extensive agriculture with a focus on water needs, water use, and impacts on water resources. Non-point sources of pollution, nutrient modelling, soil and land degradation, protection, and rehabilitation of watersheds including buffer zones, wetlands, and best management practices. Equivalency: LWS_V 520. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.

SOIL 524.faculty: Faculty of Land and Food Systems
SOIL 524.description: The theory, design and evaluation of instrumentation for biometeorological research. Prerequisite: Permission of the instructor is required. This course is not eligible for Credit/D/Fail grading.
